title: Choose Touchline's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Terrace Scarf. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Terrace Scarf
options.lineage: knitted bar scarves held up on the terraces, half-and-half matchday scarves
options.thesis: Every prediction is knitted into a scarf: a fixture is a half-and-half scarf whose seam sits at the win split, a club's season is a bar scarf of its results.
options.viewport: Standard Material shell: top bar with league chips, 4-tab navigation bar (Home, Clubs, Players, Scout). Home leads with the weekend's big fixture as a full-width half-and-half scarf: home colours left, away right, draw as a neutral knit band in the middle, each band's width = its probability, the favourite's % set monumental. Below: Trending players, Clubs in form (each a short bar scarf of W/D/L), Power rankings, Bargains, Overworked watch.
options.risk: Club colours are not in the data yet: the pipeline must add a two-tone colour pair per club (crest-derived plus a hand-checked override table). Knit texture must stay a whisper or it becomes a costume.

raised.raise: Result and risk states carry shape, not just hue: won bars knit solid, draws in a cross-stitch, losses as a dropped-stitch gap, so colour is never the only signal.
One graphic owns each screen: a single hero scarf per view, everything else quiet type on a calm ground.
Scarf lettering is a true stitch-grid display face, used only at whole-grid sizes for club names and the hero number, never for body text.
Elevation discipline: only bottom sheets float; cards sit flat on the ground with tonal surfaces, no stray shadows.

options.label: The Pink Paper
options.lineage: La Gazzetta dello Sport and the pink Saturday results editions
options.thesis: The app as Monday's pink sports paper: results and verdicts in condensed headline type on salmon-pink newsprint, tables in tight column rhythm.
options.viewport: Same Material shell on a pink ground; Home leads with a headline verdict ('City and Arsenal level at 49%') over a dense power table.
options.risk: It is the most familiar direction here and leans toward broadsheet-editorial styling, which on a working screen can read as a newspaper instead of an app.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.lineage: airport wayfinding: yellow overhead bands, monumental gate numbers
options.thesis: Each card answers one question at monumental scale, like a gate sign: one message per band, the key number huge.
options.viewport: Home as a stack of yellow bands: 'Arsenal v Leeds · 71% home win', 'Running hot: Watkins · 8 G/A in 5'.
options.case: Holds product clarity (glance-first, one answer per band) but fans don't identify with airport signage, so it loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Can feel like a utility, not a fan's app; yellow everywhere tires the eye.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrograms on a light box
options.case: Loses both: no football resonance, and hairline states are too subtle for a 30-second glance.
options.kept: State carried by form (solid, cross-stitch, dropped stitch), not hue alone.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.case: Loses both: coded labels hide the answer, the opposite of answer-first.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Loses both on its own, but knitted scarf lettering IS a bitmap.
options.kept: A stitch-grid display face at whole-grid sizes only.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Loses both: no fan resonance, and its stepped motion fights Material motion.
options.kept: Only sheets float; ply is the only rank.

options.label: Event Catalogue
options.case: Loses both: dense stamp grids overwhelm a casual glance.
options.kept: Player browse repacks in whole uniform cells.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What FotMob and Sofascore ship: dark navy cards, a green accent, dense stat lists, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Fixture list with crests and percentages, league tabs, cards stacked down the screen.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps fans already have, by design.
